analysis: Trial succeeded with host validation macro HR@10=0.6112 across 200 users per category: Movies_and_TV 0.690, Industrial_and_Scientific 0.625, Electronics 0.400, CDs_and_Vinyl 0.730. Allocated GPU time was 1140.34 seconds. Electronics remains the weakest category. Successful execution supports the revised diagnostics and serialization path, but does not establish the earlier crash’s cause or isolate the attention mechanism’s benefit. Reload predictions use numerical tolerances because CUDA sparse propagation can vary slightly; finite-output checks and traceback persistence remain enabled.
code_summary: Trains one independent LightGCN network per category, with 64-dimensional embeddings and three propagation layers over a normalized user–item graph built solely from training interactions. A jointly trained attention module summarizes up to 128 recent history events using relative positions and the propagated user query; a learned gate fuses this summary with the graph user vector. Tied item embeddings and learned item biases produce scores. Training uses prefix targets, 64 negatives excluding observed training items, cross-entropy, embedding regularization, and Adam. Validation selects one checkpoint per category by HR@10, breaking ties with NDCG@10. The generated predictor preserves category routing and loads exactly that category’s single checkpoint, recomputing attention for supplied histories.
